Criminally underrated sporty VR game. Very simple idea, hit the ball at the targets, but while progressing through the campaign it becomes obvious there is a level of skill to be achieved, which I'm glad for because I was concerned the game might end up turning out to be too easy. I can confirm that is not the case, I am stuck on the hard campaign levels right now lol.

Outside of the campaign, there is also the endless mode, which is exactly what it sounds like and I found it a lot of fun upon first playing it. There are two other versions of the endless mode that I haven't tried out though. Endless mode is also pretty great for working up a sweat if you're into that sort of thing.

Like I saw another review mention, the game takes advantage of the VR format very well: the arena is 360 degrees and builds itself around the player. I've felt pretty immersed to be honest. I think this is a title that really shows the potential of VR as a gaming platform.

In terms of multiplayer, I've only played one match, and while the player counts on steamcharts are depressing, the game is crossplay with Quest users so you'll probably run into them most of the time. A beautiful aspect of the matchmaking though is that you can queue up for a game and still go play while you wait, a feature more titles VR and otherwise need to embrace.

In short, very underrated, simple concept but still provides a challenge. I haven't been playing for very long at this point but I can already tell it's a game I'll be continuously coming back to. Also runs great on Proton if you're into that sort of thing. Buy it.

Without a doubt, Racket: Nx is the best money I've spent on a VR exclusive game. The developer claims to strive for an "unreasonable level of polish". One of my favorite things about it is that the developer gives players a monthly set to play through that always surprises with new elements and skill-building features. I've owned it for years, play for a few hours a week, and still haven't been able to complete every set in the game, let alone get every star for each set. It's challenging, fun, gorgeous, and never ceases to impress me. If you like standing VR games with a mild-moderate level of exercise, this needs to be in your library.
